metaTitle: Kando: learn a language from videos in that language
metaDescription: Kando is a free, source-available desktop app that plays videos with bilingual subtitles: it transcribes the speech on your computer and translates every line.
metaImageAlt: Kando's icon and headline beside its player, which shows a film with the original line and its translation together
ogTagline: Paste a link: Kando transcribes it on your computer and plays it with bilingual subtitles.
heroTitle:
Real videos,
understood line by line.
heroLead: Paste a YouTube or Bilibili link. Kando transcribes the speech on your computer, translates it line by line, and plays the video with the original and the translation on screen together.
heroMeta: Free · source available (FSL) · macOS, Linux, Windows, iPhone, Android · v{version}
shotPlayerAlt: The player with bilingual subtitles, and every line of the film in the side panel
sitesLead: Works with the {count} websites yt-dlp downloads from: paste a link and go
sitesStripLabel: Some of the websites Kando downloads videos from
stepsEyebrow: From a link to bilingual subtitles
stepDownloadBody: Paste a link or drop in a file. For a site you need to sign in to, sign in once in the built-in browser first.
stepTranscribeBody: The speech is recognized on your own computer, and Kando works out which language is spoken.
stepTranslateBody: Every line is translated into your language, and the model can read the lines before it for context.
stepExportBody: Two subtitle files, the original and a bilingual one, ready to watch and learn from.
libraryTitle:
Everything you're learning from,
in one place
libraryBody: A library is a `.kando` folder of ordinary files. Keep several and switch between them in the sidebar, or filter by YouTube, Bilibili, other websites and files on your computer.
libraryPoint1: Every film gets an original and a bilingual SRT beside it
libraryPoint2: Videos on your computer are transcribed where they are, never copied
libraryPoint3: Every film picks up where you stopped

detailReplayBody: Jump to the previous or next line, hear this one again, or loop it until you've got it.
detailModesBody: Bilingual, original only, translation only or off. Shift them by 0.1 seconds and change their style.
detailSearchBody: The side panel lists every line; click one to jump to it. It also cuts the film into 4 to 12 clips.
detailWhisperBody: From Tiny (77.7 MB) to Large v3 (3.1 GB): pick the one your computer runs well.
detailAIBody: EveryAPI by default, or OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Ollama and any other OpenAI-compatible API.
detailBrowserBody: Sign in to a website in Browse, and downloads from the link bar, the command line or MCP all use that sign-in.
detailUploadBody: Optional: upload the video and its bilingual subtitles to R2, S3, Alibaba Cloud OSS or Tencent Cloud COS.
detailShortcutsBody: Playback, subtitles and windows all have shortcuts. ⌘/ shows them all; ⌘K opens the command palette.
detailLanguagesBody: 简体中文, 繁體中文, English, 日本語 and 한국어, switched at any time.
openTitle: Free, with all the code on GitHub
openBody: Written in Go with a native interface, no web view. macOS, Windows and Linux all have ready-made packages, and Kando updates itself when a new version comes out.
dlMacBody: Download the arm64 .dmg for a Mac with Apple silicon or the x64 one for an Intel Mac, open it and drag Kando to Applications. It's signed and notarized by Apple.
dlFirstRun: The first time Kando opens, it downloads whichever of yt-dlp, ffmpeg and whisper.cpp are missing.
dlLinuxBody: Installs the Debian or Arch package for your computer with sudo:
dlLinuxNote: On Debian and Ubuntu you can also install the .deb with apt.
dlWinBody: Download the x64 installer for most PCs, or the arm64 one for a Windows on Arm PC, and run it. It is signed, but while its certificate is new to SmartScreen, SmartScreen may warn before it runs: choose More info, then Run anyway.
dlWinNote: On Windows Kando doesn't download yt-dlp, ffmpeg and whisper-cli yet: install them with a package manager and put them on your PATH.
dlPhoneBody: The phone app plays the films in Kando on your computer, or straight from a NAS. The Android app is on Google Play, and the iPhone app is in public beta on TestFlight.
dlIosNote: On an iPhone, install TestFlight from the App Store, then open this page on the iPhone and tap Join the TestFlight beta.
dlReadme: The full guide in the README
faqPriceA: Kando is free to use, and its source code is public under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2): anyone may read, change and run it for anything but a competing product, and each version becomes Apache 2.0 two years after its release. Translation uses an AI service, which charges as that provider does; with Ollama or LM Studio the model runs on your own computer.
faqSitesQ: Which websites does it work with?
faqSitesA: YouTube, Bilibili and the other websites yt-dlp downloads from, {count} in all; Help › Supported Websites… in the app lists them. You can also drop mp4, mov, mkv, webm and other files from your computer on the window.
faqSpeechA: On your computer, by whisper.cpp: the audio is never uploaded to be transcribed. A whisper model is downloaded from Hugging Face the first time it's used.
faqTranslateQ: What do I need for translation?
faqTranslateA: Kando translates with EveryAPI by default: sign in to EveryAPI in Settings › AI Service, or with the EveryAPI CLI (everyapi auth login). Or pick another provider there and enter its model and API key; Ollama and LM Studio need no key.
faqSystemsQ: Which systems does it run on?
faqSystemsA: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows (x86-64 and ARM64) and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64) all have ready-made packages.
faqLoginQ: What about videos you have to sign in to watch?
faqLoginA: Open the website in Browse in the sidebar and sign in; every download after that uses the sign-in. Clear Sign-in Data… signs you out of them all at once.
faqExportA: Every finished video has two SRT files beside it: the original subtitles, and bilingual ones with the translation above the original, ready for any other player.

privacyMetaDescription: How Kando's desktop and phone apps treat your data: no account, analytics or tracking. Your videos and words stay on your devices and go where you send them.
privacyLead: Kando keeps your videos, subtitles, words and notes on your own devices. We run no server that receives them, apart from EveryAPI, an AI service we run, which receives the text you send it only if you choose it as your AI service. The apps carry no analytics, advertising or tracking. This policy says what the apps send over the network, where, and when.
privacyWhoBody: Kando is made by YLDM Co., Ltd. (“we”), which is responsible for this policy. It covers Kando for macOS, Windows and Linux (the desktop app), Kando for iPhone, iPad and Android (the phone app), and this website.
privacyCollectBody:
Nothing, unless you choose EveryAPI as your AI service. There is no Kando account, and neither app sends us usage statistics, crash reports or identifiers. Your libraries, subtitles, saved words and lines, notes and settings are files on your devices.
Of the services the apps reach for you, listed below, only EveryAPI is ours: YLDM Co., Ltd. runs it, and it forwards your requests to the AI model providers it routes them to, such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. It receives the text you send it, and your EveryAPI sign-in, only when you choose it as your AI service. The other services are not ours, and we receive nothing from them.
privacyPhoneBody:
The phone app works with the computers you pair it with and sends your data nowhere else:
- Libraries, videos, subtitles, playback positions, saved words and lines, notes and reviews travel between the phone and a paired computer over your local network, by HTTPS pinned to the certificate the computer showed when you paired, so only that computer can read them.
- Away from that network, if you turn on Sync through your storage on the computer, they pass through your own S3-compatible bucket, encrypted with a key only the phone and the computer hold. The phone has no key to the bucket.
- Word lookups and explanations are asked of the paired computer, which uses the AI service you set up there. The phone reaches no AI service itself.
- The only web page the app opens is the desktop app's download page on GitHub, in your browser.
The app asks for local network access, to reach your computer, and for notifications only if you turn on the review reminder, which is scheduled on the phone.
privacyDesktopBody:
Speech recognition runs on your computer with whisper.cpp, and a library is a folder of ordinary files. The desktop app uses the network only for these:
- Downloads: when you add a link, or a subscription checks a channel, yt-dlp fetches the video, its subtitles and thumbnail from that website. A sign-in you made in Kando's browser, or in the browser you chose under Browser Sign-In, goes only to that website. Subtitles Only videos stream from the website as you watch.
- Browsing: the web pages you open in Kando.
- AI services: translation, proofreading, explanations, recaps and word lookups send subtitle text to the AI service you set up, such as EveryAPI or OpenAI, under that provider's terms. EveryAPI is run by YLDM Co., Ltd., the company that makes Kando, and passes the text on to the AI model providers it routes requests to, such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. Ollama or LM Studio on your computer keeps it there. API keys you enter stay in Kando's settings on your computer. Signing in to EveryAPI in Kando keeps its key and refresh token in the system's secure store (Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, Secret Service on Linux), or in Kando's settings file where there is none, as on a Linux session without Secret Service.
- Programs and speech models: yt-dlp, ffmpeg and whisper-cli are downloaded from GitHub, and the speech models you choose from Hugging Face or hf-mirror.com.
- Updates: once a day, and when you choose Check for Updates…, Kando reads the latest release from GitHub.
- Plugins: the plugin directory's list comes from this website, at most once a day when you open Browse Plugins…, and so do the plugins you install from it. With a script plugin installed, the list of withdrawn plugins is read from GitHub once a day. A plugin reaches only the addresses it declares and you allow.
- Upload: when you press Upload, the video goes to the object storage you set up. Signing in with Google is optional and only files uploads under your email address; it happens between your browser, Google and Kando, and the token is kept in Kando's settings on your computer.
- Phone Sync: once you turn it on, Kando serves the phones you paired on your local network, and through your own bucket if you turn on Sync through your storage.
Offline mode, in Settings › Privacy, stops all of these except Phone Sync on your local network and the daily update check. The same page lists what each step sends.
privacyFeedbackBody: Help › Send Feedback… opens a new issue on GitHub in your browser, filled in with what you wrote and the details you chose to attach, such as the versions of the app and the system. Kando first takes out file paths, the name of your home folder and anything shaped like a key or token. Nothing is sent until you submit the issue on GitHub, where it is public. Kando's log file stays on your computer.
privacyOthersBody: The websites you download from, your AI provider, your object storage, Google, GitHub and Hugging Face handle what reaches them under their own privacy policies. Apart from EveryAPI, which we run, we do not control them, and they send us nothing about you.
privacySiteBody: This website is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from other websites. It remembers the language you choose in your browser's local storage, which stays in your browser. GitHub, as the host, may log visitors' IP addresses under the GitHub Privacy Statement.
privacyChoicesBody: Unless you use EveryAPI, we hold no data about you, so there is nothing for us to access, correct or delete. If you do, we hold your EveryAPI account and its usage records, which you can ask us about at the address below. Your data is in your hands: delete videos and libraries in the app, uninstall it, unpair a phone or a computer to stop all transfers, sign out of Google, or turn on offline mode.
privacyChildrenBody: Kando collects no personal information from anyone, children included.
privacyChangesBody: If the apps start sending something new, we will update this page and its date. Earlier versions are in the history of Kando's repository on GitHub.
privacyContactBody: YLDM Co., Ltd. answers questions and requests about privacy at:
